title: Redis cache vs DB read replica vs CDN caching
description: Three derived-read options. None of them is the TokenX ledger. Freshness, key, and failure behavior decide which hop is legal.

cells.workload: Hot derived keys: session, feature flags, campaign metadata, rate-limit counters. Application owns fill and invalidation.
cells.consistency: Stale until TTL or explicit delete. No replica-apply position. A hit can be wrong after a primary write.
cells.latency: Sub-ms to low-ms in-region for GET. Stampede on miss if uncoordinated.
cells.scaling: Shard by key. Memory-bound. Replicas are async and optional.
cells.failure: Flush, eviction, or process restart can empty the cache. Persistence does not make it a system of record. Sentinel/cluster split-brain is an ops failure, not a feature.
cells.costOps: Memory is expensive. You operate eviction policy, key design, and stampede control (singleflight).
cells.whenNot: Spendable balances, unique allocation, or any read that must match the latest committed primary without a version token.

cells.workload: Same SQL model as the primary, offloading stale-tolerant queries and reports. Still relational/item-shaped like the primary.
cells.consistency: Applied WAL/LSN on a named timeline. Read-your-writes needs a position token; equal numeric LSNs on different timelines are not comparable.
cells.latency: Similar to primary for indexed reads plus replication lag (ms to seconds under load).
cells.scaling: Add replicas until WAL apply, connections, or lag saturate. Does not scale writes.
cells.failure: Lag, WAL recycle forcing rebuild, or accidental dual-primary if promoted without fencing.
cells.costOps: Extra instances plus replication bandwidth. You still vacuum and monitor apply lag.
cells.whenNot: When you needed write scale, or when the session requires linearizable/read-your-writes and you will not wait for apply or go to the primary.

cells.workload: Public or versioned GET bytes: images, immutable API responses, CSS/JS, downloadable objects. Close to the user.
cells.consistency: TTL, cache-control, and surrogate keys. No per-user read-your-writes unless you bypass. Shared caches can leak if Vary/auth is wrong.
cells.latency: Tens of ms at edge on hit. Origin miss adds the full origin path.
cells.scaling: Edge fan-out. Origin shield protects the primary. Purge is eventually consistent across POPs.
cells.failure: Poisoned content until purge, origin outage (stale-if-error is a choice), or TLS/cert issues.
cells.costOps: Egress and request billing. Cache-key design is the operator burden.
cells.whenNot: Authenticated ledger reads, per-user private data without a correct cache key, or writes. Do not put TokenX transfers on a CDN.

assumptions: Cache-aside: app reads Redis, on miss reads primary, then SET. No write-through claimed unless you add it.
Replica: PostgreSQL-class streaming replication, asynchronous unless a cell says synchronous commit.
CDN: HTTP GET with explicit Cache-Control. Authenticated content is opt-in and easy to get wrong.
All three hops are derived relative to the primary store for that resource.
